cards.q: What is Git and why do network engineers use it?
cards.a: Git is a distributed version control system that tracks configs, scripts, and playbooks and enables branches, commits, and rollback. It is the backbone of Infrastructure as Code and config-as-code workflows, giving a safety net for network config changes.

cards.q: What are the benefits of using Git?
cards.a: Versioning (track changes), rollback (revert errors), branching (parallel work), collaboration (team/PR), and audit (history).

cards.q: What are the three states of a Git file?
cards.a: working (your files), staged (in the index), and committed (in the repository). Files flow from modified to staged to committed.

cards.q: What do the core Git commands do?
cards.a: git init starts a repo, git add stages, git commit saves a snapshot, git status shows state, git log shows history, git checkout switches/restores, and git push/pull sync with remotes. add then commit records a change; push/pull syncs.

cards.q: What is the difference between git add and git commit?
cards.a: git add stages file changes into the index; git commit saves a permanent snapshot of the staged changes in the repository. git diff shows the changes and git log shows history.

cards.q: How does Git support networking config-as-code?
cards.a: Config files and Ansible/Terraform playbooks are versioned in Git, which gives audit and rollback, and collaboration happens through PR review. Storing configs/playbooks in Git makes them reproducible.

cards.q: How do remote workflows and branch/PR collaboration work?
cards.a: Remotes like GitHub/GitLab hold cloned repositories; you create a feature branch, commit, then merge via a pull request. Branch plus PR keeps changes reviewable.

cards.q: How do you troubleshoot common Git problems?
cards.a: Nothing to commit = files not staged (git add); merge conflict = check git status; wrong branch = git checkout/branch; remote failures = auth (git remote); lost changes = uncommitted work (git stash).

cards.q: What is the order of file states in Git?
cards.a: A file moves from working (modified) to staged (in the index) to committed (snapshot in the repository); git add stages it and git commit saves it.

cards.q: Which commands show change history and the diff of changes?
cards.a: git log shows commit history and git diff shows the exact changes; git status shows the current state of the working tree and index.
